strategy_analysis:
A-B: paragraph chunking raises dev Hit@3 from 10/15 to 12/15 and Hit@1 from 7/15 to 12/15, but increases chunk count from 241 to 271. B has fewer total characters/tokens because it has no overlap; long paragraphs and running headers still produce fragmented or unhelpful chunks. On the fixed 10 anchors, AI coherence is 1.00/2 for A and 1.60/2 for B/C.

B-C: retrieval metrics are equal on both splits. On filtered dev q08, B retrieves chapters [2,1,2] while C retrieves [2,2,2], improving dev filter compliance from 1/2 to 2/2. All five test top-3 lists are identical for B/C. Metadata helps enforce scope but does not improve Hit@3 here, and a valid chapter filter does not remove same-chapter header-only chunks.

C was selected before test because B/C tie on dev hits and C mean SQL search is 10.5848 ms versus 10.6482 ms for B, a difference of about 0.0634 ms. This is a noisy timing tie-break, not evidence of a general speed advantage; query order and warm caches can affect it.

Test Hit@3 favors A (4/5) over B/C (3/5); retain C as the dev-selected configuration. AI grounding reads enough combined evidence in all five test cases, even where the strict single-quote metric misses. q18 uses a short inference from definitions rather than the direct recommendation; author review is especially important for this label. Do not retrospectively change frozen gold or relabel the primary metric using AI scores. A future human-confirmed equivalent-evidence metric may be reported separately without hiding these original counts.
